result_text:
The four broken default conventions now match what they were meant for, and a new test covers them. The new `ScopingConventionsTest` and the existing `SourceFileFilterTest` pass offline (9 tests, 0 failures).

Changes are in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **pkgdown, Doxygen and meta-generator rules:** the path pattern was `(html|html|xhtml)`, a typo for `(html|htm|xhtml)`. Now `.htm` pages match, and `.html` and `.xhtml` still do.
- **.NET doc XML rule:** path `.*/[.]xml` became `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches. The `<doc>` content check is unchanged.
- **`// Generated by …` JavaScript rule:** path `.*/[.]js` became `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches.
- **Gradle JavaScript rule:** path `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` became `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches. `build.gradle` is still matched by its own rule.

I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It checks that the fixed files land in the right scope and that the previously matched files still do. It also checks that a hand-written `.htm`, a `settings.xml` without `<doc>`, a hand-written `app.js` and an `app.js` in the build scope stay out.

I did not commit anything. I did not confirm that the new test fails on the original code; the `.htm` and `.xml` cases would have failed there by reading the patterns.
